overview: The Medford Zoning Board of Appeals is a public municipal body responsible for adjudicating petitions for dimensional variances, special permits, site plan reviews, administrative zoning appeals, and Chapter 40B comprehensive permit applications. Operating across 76 recorded meetings between April 2022 and October 2026, the board evaluates proposed residential expansions, commercial redevelopments, multi-family housing projects, and retail cannabis dispensaries. Throughout this period, the board conducted extensive peer-reviewed public hearings for major Chapter 40B housing developments while resolving local setback, lot area, and use variance requests. As of the most recent meeting in October 2026, the board evaluated protected accessory dwelling unit proposals under updated state guidelines, approved special permits and variances for residential alterations and demolitions, and extended relief for a long-standing mixed-use redevelopment.

threads.name: 4000 Mystic Valley Parkway 40B Comprehensive Permit
threads.summary: In late 2022, the board reopened public hearings for a Chapter 40B comprehensive permit petition proposing a 350-unit residential development at 4000 Mystic Valley Parkway [M10#1]. Over numerous sessions in early 2023, the board and peer review consultants evaluated civil engineering, traffic impacts, site circulation, building massing, and fire safety protocols for wood-frame construction [M13#2, M16#1, M28#2]. In July 2023, the board formally approved the comprehensive permit, incorporating conditions for linkage fee waivers, fire safety occupancy plans, and public art [M32#1, M32#5, M32#7]. In October 2024, the board determined that subsequent design refinements to external access and rooftop amenities constituted insubstantial changes under 40B regulations [M59#2].

threads.name: 970 Fellsway Chapter 40B Permit and Lot Split
threads.summary: The board initiated comprehensive permit hearings for a 289-unit Chapter 40B housing development at 970 Fellsway in late 2023 [M37#2]. In early 2024, the applicant submitted revised alternative concept plans stepping down building heights near residential neighbors and increasing public green space [M40#1, M41#1]. Following comprehensive civil engineering and traffic peer reviews [M47#1, M51#2], the board approved the 40B comprehensive permit in May 2024 alongside a partial linkage fee waiver for off-site infrastructure improvements [M54#3]. In January 2025, the board granted a special permit to demolish a section of an adjacent commercial building to execute a lot split supporting the approved residential development [M61#2].

threads.name: 590 Boston Avenue Mixed-Use Redevelopment
threads.summary: In July 2022, the board granted a 12-month extension for a special permit and variance to replace a gas station at 590 Boston Avenue with a 40-unit mixed-use building [M04#1]. The board approved additional six-month extensions in January 2023 [M12#3] and January 2024 [M38#2]. In November 2023, the board approved plan modifications increasing the residential unit count to 45 and reconfiguring parking to an at-grade design [M36#2]. The board granted a further two-year extension for the variance and special permit in October 2026 [M76#2].

threads.name: Cannabis Dispensary and Delivery Special Permits
threads.summary: The board granted a special permit and site plan approval for Theory Wellness to open a retail dispensary at 162 Mystic Avenue in August 2022 [M05#5], later expanding the permit to include medical cannabis sales in February 2026 [M68#4]. In April 2023, the board approved a retail dispensary special permit for New England Organics at 114 Mystic Avenue [M22#2]. In May 2026, the board approved medical cannabis sales and manufacturing for Victory Gardens at 114 Mystic Avenue [M71#2], followed by approval of a cannabis delivery courier special permit at the location in July 2026 [M73#1].

threads.name: Accessory Dwelling Unit (ADU) Relief under State Law
threads.summary: In July 2026, the board continued petitions for attic expansions to create accessory dwelling units at 1-3 Vassar Street and 12 Wellesley Street to seek municipal legal advice on newly enacted state ADU legislation [M73#3, M73#4]. The cases were continued through September 2026 while the board evaluated modified building scale and design requirements [M75#1]. In October 2026, the board ruled that variances were not required under state law for protected ADUs and issued site-specific findings and special permits allowing the dimensional relief for both properties [M76#3, M76#4].

threads.name: 280 Mystic Avenue 40B Comprehensive Permit
threads.summary: The board opened hearings on a Chapter 40B comprehensive permit application for a proposed 378-unit residential development at 280 Mystic Avenue in April 2024, authorizing peer review consultants [M50#1]. In May 2024, the board voted to require peer review fee payments, citing a lack of responsiveness from the applicant [M54#2]. The applicant formally requested to withdraw the comprehensive permit petition in June 2024, which the board accepted without prejudice [M55#2].

periods.narrative: The board conducted extensive peer reviews for large-scale Chapter 40B proposals on the Fellsway and Mystic Avenue, approved commercial auto dealership height modifications, and navigated board leadership transitions.

The board ruled on administrative zoning violation appeals, authorized new medical cannabis and delivery services, and established local procedures for reviewing protected accessory dwelling units under state law.
